predecessors.name: Russian Republic
predecessors.text: 'the governorates of Volyn, Kiev, Podillia, Chernihiv, Poltava, Kharkiv, Katerynoslav, Kherson and Taurida (except of Crimea)' named in the Third Universal of 20 November 1917

successors.name: Ukrainian Soviet Socialist Republic
successors.text: the Ukrainian land held by the Bolsheviks after the collapse of the UPR; the page's infobox: 'Succeeded by Ukrainian SSR (1919)'

ledger.x: 1917, 20 November (7 November O.S.): the Central Rada's Third Universal proclaims the Ukrainian People's Republic, still as autonomy 'within the Russian Republic'.
1918, January: the Bolsheviks take Kyiv from the Rada.
1918, January: Bolshevik forces take the left bank and the Dnieper bend.
1918, 9 February: Muravyov's Bolshevik forces take Kyiv.
1918, 3 March: Soviet Russia gives up Ukraine at Brest-Litovsk.
1918, 1 March: the Ukrainian army returns to Kyiv.
1918, 29 April: Skoropadsky's coup turns the republic into the Ukrainian State (Hetmanate).
1918, December: the Directorate overthrows the Hetmanate and restores the Ukrainian People's Republic.
1919, 3 January: the Red Army takes Kharkiv.
1919, 22 January: the republic and the West Ukrainian People's Republic unite.
1919, January: the Red Army takes Poltava and Yekaterinoslav.
1919, 5 February: the Bolsheviks take Kyiv and the long fight for Ukraine begins.
1919, 5 February: the Bolsheviks take Kyiv again.
1919, March: the Bolsheviks overrun the rest of central and eastern Ukraine.
1921, 18 March: the Peace of Riga closes the fighting for the UPR.
1921: the Ukrainian People's Republic ends as a state on Ukrainian soil.

wars.name: Ukrainian-Soviet War
wars.outcome: The Bolsheviks took Kyiv in the winter of 1918, were driven out on 1 March 1918 with German help, and took it again on 5 February 1919; the Peace of Riga (18 March 1921) left the UPR without land and its government in exile.

wars.name: Polish-Soviet War (UPR as Poland's ally)
wars.outcome: On 22 April 1920 'Ukrainian representative Andriy Livytskyi signed the Treaty of Warsaw'; on 25 April 'Polish troops supported by two Ukrainian divisions' attacked.

certainty.note: Claims and shifting fronts; the only line on the pages is the 'preliminary demarcation line with the Russian SFSR' of 1918, which the page does not place.
